title: Tensor and Cartesian base-change compatibility for exceptional coefficient mates
statement: The tensor compatibility and Cartesian base-change compatibility conjuncts of exceptional coefficient comparison, under the same hypotheses as the parent theorem.

source.place: Projection, open/proper exchange, and mate calculations in compatibility (3).

proof.text: Express the smooth tensor map using the ordered projection isomorphism and canonical derived symmetry. Transpose the coefficient square through the target exceptional adjunction. Apply the component projection/evaluation transport lemma to compact-scalar projection coherence, the normalized scalar right-unit component, and the specified tensor-domain formula; recover the desired mate square by the adjunction Hom bijection.

For base change, the existing domain theorem puts G_A K in bounded-constructible finite-Tor objects. Apply the Tor lower bound to the scalar coefficient sheaf and transport it through scalarTensorIso. Exact scalar restriction commutes with homology and is faithful, so it reflects the resulting lower bound for scalar extension. Exact/left-derived inverse-image identifications transport compact-support scalar base change to the inverse compact-support exchange cube.

The exceptional maps and beta are the specified counit transposes. Apply the generic coefficient-exchange mate theorem at G_A K to the preceding cube. Its equality is exactly BaseChangeCompatibility. Combine it with tensor compatibility.

proof_origin.place: Compatibility (3), tensor and mixed Cartesian squares.
